items.markdown:
The best treatment for moderate eczema in kids is `a daily routine of thick, fragrance-free moisturizers combined with prescription mid-strength [12] topical corticosteroids or non-steroid creams` [12] to control flare-ups.[[1]](https://happyskindermatology.com/2025/03/07/best-products-for-eczema-treatment-for-infants/)[[2]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8128359/)[[3]](https://paedicare.com.au/eczema-children/)

### Daily Skin Care Routine

- **Emollients (Moisturizers):** Apply thick creams or ointments (like CeraV e or Aquaphor ) multiple times a day and immediately after bathing to lock in water.
- **Bathing:** Give your child short, lukewarm baths using soap-free, fragrance-free cleansers, then gently pat the skin dry.[[1]](https://www.akronchildrens.org/kidshealth/en/parents/eczema-atopic-dermatitis.html)[[2]](https://a-zpeds.com/managing-childhood-eczema-in-the-preschool-years/)[[3]](https://www.citymd.com/health-and-wellness/sensitive-skin-sos-a-comprehensive-guide-to-eczema-in-children)[[4]](https://mydoctor.kaiserpermanente.org/mas/structured-content/Condition_Eczema_Derm.xml?co=%2Fregions%2Fmas)[[5]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DId8ky-76hA&t=119)

### Medical Treatments for Flares

- **Topical Corticosteroids:** A doctor may prescribe a moderate-strength prescription steroid cream or ointment to reduce redness and swelling during a flare.[[1]](https://ubiehealth.com/doctors-note/eczema-rash-flare-persists-causes-relief-action-57)[[2]](https://www.brooklynbridgepediatrics.com/medical-conditions/eczema-atopic-dermatitis-and-your-child)
- **Topical Calcineurin Inhibitors:** Non-steroid prescription creams [12] (like tacrolimus or pimecrolimus) can treat sensitive areas like the face or neck without the risk of skin thinning from long-term steroid use.[[1]](https://www.citymd.com/health-and-wellness/sensitive-skin-sos-a-comprehensive-guide-to-eczema-in-children)
- **Wet Wrap Therapy:** Damp cotton layers wrapped over moisturizers and medication can soothe severe or stubborn flare-ups.[[1]](https://a-zpeds.com/managing-childhood-eczema-in-the-preschool-years/)[[2]](https://www.citymd.com/health-and-wellness/sensitive-skin-sos-a-comprehensive-guide-to-eczema-in-children)

### Managing Triggers

- **Clothing:** Dress your child in soft, breathable cotton and avoid scratchy wool or polyester.
- **Nails:** Keep your child's fingernails short or use cotton mittens at night to prevent skin damage and secondary infection from scratching.
- **Environment:** Identify and avoid known irritants such as scented soaps, harsh laundry detergents, or extreme temperature changes.[[1]](https://mydoctor.kaiserpermanente.org/mas/structured-content/Condition_Eczema_Derm.xml?co=%2Fregions%2Fmas)[[2]](https://www.akronchildrens.org/kidshealth/en/parents/eczema-atopic-dermatitis.html)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DId8ky-76hA&t=119)[[4]](https://a-zpeds.com/managing-childhood-eczema-in-the-preschool-years/)[[5]](https://www.citymd.com/health-and-wellness/sensitive-skin-sos-a-comprehensive-guide-to-eczema-in-children)
